# 1 Clement Chapter 23 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 23 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_023_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 23

**23:1** Our Father is full of mercy and kindness. He shows compassion to those who reverence him, and he generously pours out his grace on all who come to him with an honest heart.

**23:2** So let us not be half-hearted or allow our souls to be fed by empty hopes about his magnificent gifts.

**23:3** Let us have nothing to do with the scripture that says: "How miserable are the wavering—those who doubt within themselves and say: 'We heard all this back in our fathers' day, and now we're getting old, and none of it has come true for us.'"

**23:4** You fools! Look at a tree—take a grapevine for example. First it drops its leaves, then a shoot appears, then leaves, then blossoms, and after that an unripe berry, and finally a full ripe cluster. In just a short time the fruit reaches full maturity.

**23:5** In the same way, God's purpose will be fulfilled quickly and suddenly. As scripture bears witness: "He will come and will not delay; the Lord will come suddenly to his temple—the Holy One you are waiting for."

---

*PNEUMA renders for contemporary clarity, preserving the rhetorical urgency of Clement's anti-doubt argument.*
